title: The beginning of wisdom (Proverbs 1:7; 3:5–6)
hook: trust in the Lord with all your heart and lean not on your own understanding

segments.voice: Yesterday, the end of Job: he prayed for the friends who hurt him, and his daughters got names and land. Your line was pray for the friends. Did you wish someone one good thing? Day four hundred fifty.

Three words most adults find surprisingly hard to say: I don't know. We'll guess, bluff, change the subject, or look it up under the table before we admit it. There's a reason. Not knowing feels like weakness. Yet almost everyone has met the opposite kind of person, the doctor, the grandmother, the mechanic, who says I don't know easily and somehow becomes more trustworthy for it. Today we open the book of Proverbs, a collection of sayings about how to live well. And its first big idea isn't about being clever. It's about where wisdom starts.
screen: `I DON'T KNOW.` → `HARDER THAN IT SOUNDS.` → `WHERE WISDOM STARTS.`

segments.voice: Proverbs opens with a heading: "The proverbs of Solomon the son of David, king of Israel." But inside, other collections carry other names: sayings copied by the men of King Hezekiah, the words of Agur, the words of King Lemuel. It's a library of sayings gathered over generations. Then comes the motto for the whole book, in the King James Bible: "The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction." You heard nearly the same line at the end of Job's poem on wisdom. The Hebrew word for beginning is reshit, the same word hidden in the Bible's first line, in the beginning. It can mean the starting point, and also the first and best part. Awe of God isn't the finish line of wisdom. It's the first step, and the foundation. Now today's word. Wisdom in Hebrew is chokhmah, and it's surprisingly practical. The same word describes the skill of the craftsmen who built the tabernacle in Exodus, people filled with wisdom to work in gold and wood and cloth. Wisdom is know-how. Skill at living. And in Proverbs, wisdom is pictured as a woman who stands in the street and calls out to anyone passing. Then chapter three: "Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths." Lean not doesn't mean stop thinking. Proverbs is full of hard thinking. It means don't put your whole weight on it, like a walking stick that might snap. Directing paths, in Hebrew, means making them straight.
screen: `A LIBRARY OF SAYINGS` · `RESHIT: FIRST STEP, FIRST PART` · `CHOKHMAH: SKILL AT LIVING` · `DON'T PUT YOUR WHOLE WEIGHT ON IT` · then, large: `TRUST IN THE LORD WITH ALL THINE HEART.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: admit one thing you don't know. Sit, and settle. Think of a question in your life you've been pretending to have answered. How a relationship will turn out. Whether a decision was right. What a person really meant. Something about God. Name it plainly to yourself: I don't know. Notice how that feels in your chest. Then breathe, and let it be okay not to know for these two minutes. If you pray, you can say the line: trust in the Lord with all thine heart. If you don't, simply rest your weight on something other than having the answer. The bell holds the time.
Wisdom. In Hebrew, chokhmah: skill at living, the know-how of a craftsman, which Proverbs says begins in awe of God.
Your line: lean not on your own. Today, say I don't know out loud once, when it's true, and see what happens next. Day four hundred fifty.

howItsDone: Many Christians memorize Proverbs 3:5–6 and pray it before decisions, and some read one chapter of Proverbs a day, one for each day of the month.

fork.setup: you're compiling a book of wisdom for young people. what do you put first, as the motto?
options: the fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge.
fork.reveal: Proverbs 1:7. awe of God is the first step and foundation, before any of the practical advice.

original.note: Hebrew: wisdom, skill. also used for the craftsmen who built the tabernacle.

trapdoor: what you thought: wisdom means being clever or knowing a lot.
what it means: practical skill at living, which starts in awe of God and doesn't lean its whole weight on itself.
what a scholar hears: chokhmah is craftsman's skill (Exodus 31:3), and reshit, beginning, is the word inside Genesis 1:1's bereshit.
recall: the Psalms as a mirror for the soul
keep, six times in eight verses

notes: Reshit as both 'beginning' and 'first/best part' (e.g. firstfruits). Confirm.
Chokhmah used of Bezaleel and the craftsmen (Exodus 31:3, 6; 35:31). Confirm.
'Make straight' as a sense of yashar in 3:6. Confirm.
howItsDone: the custom of reading one chapter of Proverbs daily (31 chapters) is a popular modern practice; confirm phrasing.
